Article Title: Shubman Gill's straight talk: Mohammed Siraj dropped on form, calls out saliva ban and lifeless pitch at Basin Reserve
Article Text:
Captain Shubman Gill speaks after the end of Day 5 in Wellington. (Photo: Sahil Malhotra)

Teams should be allowed to use saliva. It was a rule that was made effective during COVID. I think we are long past that. Shubman Gill

India's Prasidh Krishna, right, celebrates with teammates after taking the wicket of New Zealand's Rachin Ravindra during the fifth day of the first cricket test match in Wellington, New Zealand. (AP/PTI)(AP11_23_2026_000001A) *** Local Caption ***

'Not a great Test wicket'

When we started playing the Test match, we thought there will be a lot more in the wicket. I think on Day 3, 4 and 5, it just went flatter and flatter. Shubman Gill

WELLINGTON: Shubman Gill didn't hold back when he was asked whether Ravindra Jadeja and Mohammed Siraj 's accuracy could have made a difference at Basin Reserve. He bluntly said, "I don't think so." Right before the query, the India captain had explained at length why Siraj wasn't considered for the Playing XI in the series opener and asserted how current form played a major part in the "very tough decision"."Siraj is a great player and a great bowler that has done very well for India. Before all of that, he's a really good friend of mine. We made our debuts together. Even before playing for India, we were really good friends. So leaving him behind was actually a very tough decision for him and for me as well. But sometimes you have to see which bowlers are in the form, which bowlers are bowling the best."I told him before the match that he's going to be missing out this match. And I don't know if he agreed or not, but he understood that. He understood what was the logic behind it. He understood why we picked someone else ahead of him. And I think in every player's career or life, there comes a phase where you're not going to be at the peak of your career all the time. And I think he understands that," Gill told reporters after the first Test between India and New Zealand ended in a draw on Day 5.Siraj's exclusion was the hottest topic across platforms for the last few days, and it gathered more steam after the result didn't go India's way.Gill, however, seemed absolutely convinced with the call he made. India controlled most periods of play in the Test, but New Zealand's resistance on the final day denied them a win.The Indian captain's explanation regarding Siraj wasn't the only straightforward comment of the day, as he minced no words in calling out the quality of the ball and the saliva ban. Gill highlighted that it was an issue in England last year too."Teams should be allowed to use saliva. It was a rule that was made effective during COVID. I think we are long past that," said Gill."If you're not shining the ball or if you're not able to maintain the ball well, especially on wickets like these, it makes the job of the bowler very difficult. And also, the condition of the balls has not been too great lately. We had the same problem in England as well. We understand, after 50 overs, the ball will obviously go soft. But if the ball is going soft after 25-30 overs or it's going out of shape and you're also not able to maintain the ball and use saliva, then it's a very difficult job for the bowlers," he added.India have had to settle for draws in their last two Tests, against Sri Lanka in Colombo and New Zealand in Wellington, and on both occasions, the pitches offered no assistance to the bowlers. India toiled hard and long to take the remaining five New Zealand wickets, but the moment it didn't look possible, the hands were shaken to settle for a draw. Basin Reserve is famous for being a fast bowler's paradise, but the conditions were a stark contrast to what one had expected in the build-up, especially after the lushness on the opening day.Yes, the clear skies and bright sunshine played their part, but the moment the pitch turned from green to brown, and factoring in the quality of the ball, the edges stopped carrying. Both teams resorted to keeping the wicketkeeper up, aiming for an LBW or bowled dismissal, as conventional edged-and-gone dismissals seemed highly unlikely."When we started playing the Test match, we thought there will be a lot more in the wicket. I think on Day 3, 4 and 5, it just went flatter and flatter. There were no scallops in the wicket. There was no impact of the overs being bowled on the wicket, or even the days being played. The wicket just got slower. So having seen that, I think it was not a great Test wicket, especially if you want results. But having said that, like I said before, now because we talk about results a lot more because of the WTC, before, draws were a lot more common.So people didn't talk about draws as much," said Gill.India's bowlers collectively sent down 241 overs in the match, and even though they didn't earn the crucial World Test Championship points, captain Gill was very pleased with the group's energy and body language. With just three days between the two games, one of which is a travel day, the Indian team has cancelled its team activity before the Christchurch fixture and hopes to recharge and refresh as its hunt for crucial points continues.
Article Summary: India captain Shubman Gill spoke after the end of Day 5 in Wellington. India toiled hard and long to take the remaining five New Zealand wickets. India controlled most periods of play in the Test, but New Zealand's resistance on the final day denied them a win.

Article Title: 'Where is Kuldeep Yadav or Manav Suthar?': Sourav Ganguly questions India's team selection after Wellington draw
Article Text:
Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar (Image credit: BCCI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former India captain Sourav Ganguly has questioned India's decision to leave out specialist spinners Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar from the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington. While praising India's batting performances in the opening Test of the two-match series, Ganguly stressed that having a genuine spinner is a must to win Test matches overseas, especially on pitches that become flatter as a match progresses.His comments came after India were held to a draw by New Zealand in the first Test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. India had declared their first innings at a massive 720/9 and were in a strong position to push for victory, but could not take the remaining five wickets on the final day.New Zealand had resumed the day at 119/2, still 233 runs behind. However, the hosts showed great patience to finish at 239/5 after 120 overs. Captain Shubman Gill shook hands with the opposition batters with less than an hour left in the match.Daryl Mitchell remained unbeaten on 49 off 186 balls, while Glenn Phillips scored an unbeaten 26 off 126 deliveries. The pair batted patiently to keep India's bowlers at bay and secure a draw.In a post on X, Ganguly praised India's performances in both white-ball and red-ball cricket during the tour. However, he questioned the team's decision to play without a specialist spinner, naming Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar.“India has been brilliant this series .. white ball and now red ball .. the batting application looked super .. but they must understand to win test matches away a genuine spinner is a must on pitches which get flat with time ..u have to play one in test cricket .. Washington can play as an allrounder ..@bcci where is Kuldeep or Manav sutar ?,” Ganguly wrote.Ganguly's comments highlighted the importance of having a specialist spinner alongside Washington Sundar, who played as an all-rounder. India went into the Wellington Test with four fast bowlers — Jasprit Bumrah, Prasidh Krishna, Akash Deep and Anshul Kamboj - while leaving out Ravindra Jadeja.The decision to leave out Jadeja also raised questions among cricket experts.Kuldeep was initially part of India's Test squad but was released to play domestic cricket. Gurnoor Brar was later added to the squad. Kuldeep had played the fourth ODI against New Zealand before the Test series, conceding 73 runs in his eight overs.Suthar, who made his Test debut against Afghanistan earlier this year, was also not part of the squad. He picked up seven wickets in that match and had earlier played an important role in India's 1-0 series win over Sri Lanka, taking 16 wickets across two matches.India also left out Mohammed Siraj from the playing XI for the Wellington Test.India will now face New Zealand in the second and final Test at Hagley Oval in Christchurch, starting November 27.
Article Summary: India were held to a draw by New Zealand in the first Test at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. Sourav Ganguly questioned the team's decision to leave out specialist spinners Kuldeep Yadav and Manav Suthar. Ganguly stressed that having a genuine spinner is a must to win Test matches overseas, especially on pitches that become flatter as a match progresses.

Article Title: 'I had no idea RCB would retain me': Yash Dayal on franchise's faith after a difficult year
Article Text:
Yash Dayal (BCCI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

MUMBAI: Expressing his gratitude to Royal Challengers Bengaluru, who recently kept faith in him by confirming his retention at Rs 5 crore on Nov 17 as part of a 20-player core, despite his troubles in the last one year, Yash Dayal has promised to give it his all to his franchise in IPL- 2027."It's a very big thing for me. I had no idea that the RCB would retain me. The RCB retained me and showed faith in me. So, I will try my best to do well for them. With whatever experience I have, I will try my 100 % to do my best this season," Dayal told TOI in an interview on Sunday night, soon after taking two for 29 in four overs to play a key role in Uttar Pradesh's 12-run win over defending champions Jharkhand in the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy.The left-arm pace bowler had taken 13 wickets in 15 matches at 36.15, at an economy rate of 9.59, contributing well in RCB's maiden title triumph in 2025, but had to miss out playing in IPL-2026 after being entangled in a couple of legal cases.Dayal naturally badly missed playing cricket in what was surely the most difficult phase of his life. "Obviously, when you have your own players and watch matches on TV, it feels bad to sit at home.But it's okay. I can play now," he said.Dayal is understandably relishing playing again in domestic tournaments for UP. "Yes, I am enjoying it. I just want to play cricket. Cricket is everything for me. I don't care if I win or lose. My performance doesn't matter. I just want to enjoy my life, and cricket is my life," the fast bowler stressed.Dayal still hasn't given up on his dream to wear the India cap one day. "My ultimate goal is to represent India. I am 28 years old. I want to play for India as soon as possible. I want to forget all the years that I have missed. So, I just want to make it happen, no matter how long it isDuring a tumultuous phase in his life, Dayal married social media influencer Shweta Pundir. The left-arm quick said that marriage has made him concentrate more on cricket now. "I have become well-centered. I am trying to focus only on the game," he said.After missing out on a season of cricket due to legal cases against him that have been reportedly closed, Dayal looks intent to make up for lost time.In the four matches that he has played in the Syed Mushtaq Ali T20 Trophy for Uttar Pradesh, the left-arm fast bowler has picked up six wickets at 22.66, with an economy rate of 9.71.On Sunday, Dayal provided fine support to veteran seamer Bhuvneshwar Kumar , who took three for 39, to help UP pull off a win over Jharkhand"Overall, I bowled well. In the beginning, I was trying to pitch the ball a little ahead, but it wasn't happening that way. But as I was discussing with Kuldeep (Yadav) and Bhuvibhai, whatever you have to plan at the last minute, there should be clarity in it. So, I executed that clarity and it felt good," Dayal analysed.The seamer, who has taken 72 wickets in 75 T20 matchesat30.09, with an economy rate of 8.76, is learning a lot while bowling in tandem with 'swing king' Bhuvneshwar in SMAT. "When you are standing at the other end, or fielding somewhere, you see his field settings, what line is bowling, what shots the batters are hitting (off his bowling) you get to learn a lot from that. He has a lot of experience," Bhuvneshwar said.Years of success in the IPL-he has played 43 matches for Gujarat Titans and then RCB, in which he has taken 41 wicketsat33.90, at an economy rate of 9.57, has clearly helped Dayal understand what is required to survive as a bowler in this format. "I am still learning. I can't say that I have become very smart. I just focus on the changes I have to make match by match and according to the format," Dayal said.Bowling for RCB at ground with small dimensions like the Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru is not an easy task, but Dayal takes it as "challenge.""It's tough to bowl on small grounds like the Chinnaswamy and the Wankhede Stadium. You have to see where the batsman is playing the shot. Where can I bowl? What field can I take? Different grounds have different experiences. I have tried to apply what is required at the Chinnaswamy Stadium as a bowler. When you take the ball and mark your run up, you see that the boundary is close to you. So it is difficult to save runs. But I enjoy that challenge a lot," explained the pacer.Dayal is constantly looking to evolve as a bowler. "I have worked on overall lengths. I have worked on my yorker, bouncer and the length Ball. I am also working on my slower delivery. I am also thinking about what else I can produce," he said.
Article Summary: Yash Dayal has promised to give it his all to his franchise in IPL- 2027. Royal Challengers Bengaluru confirmed his retention at Rs 5 crore on Nov 17. The left- arm pace bowler had taken 13 wickets in 15 matches at 36.15, at an economy rate of 9.59, contributing well in RCB's maiden title triumph in 2025.

Article Title: New Zealand's blockathon frustrates India as Wellington Test ends in a draw
Article Text:

WELLINGTON: India took five New Zealand wickets in their first innings using just 28.2 overs. They needed the same number of wickets to force a result in the second innings and had around 10 more overs to play with, but they couldn't finish the job as New Zealand resisted for a well-fought draw. The afternoon of Day 5 was nowhere near as spicy as the morning on the opening day, but the visitors were still in a better position to push for crucial World Test Championship (WTC) points, which they failed to secure.India did a commendable job in the first session, removing the set pair of Devon Conway and Rachin Ravindra and sending back Tom Blundell before he could do any considerable damage. There was a lot of drama around the Blundell review because Rishabh Pant didn't feel anything, but the men in catching positions and captain Shubman Gill were convinced they had heard something. A little spike was enough to overturn the umpire's call, and India had their tails up, with Gill breaking into a little Bhangra of his own.Around that time, even the wind had picked up, and cloud cover replaced the bright sunshine, but the lifeless pitch wasn't ready to offer anything to the bowlers. The wind, blowing from the north, grew in intensity as the game progressed, with strong gusts reaching the 50 mph mark.It offered Washington Sundar considerable drift and allowed him to attack with four men in catching positions around the bat, but except for Conway's wicket, the off-spinner was safely negotiated by the hosts.Usual suspects Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips combined and were rock solid during their 63-run stand. More than the runs, it was the 253 deliveries they consumed and how they started a blockathon to eat time and secure the most favourable result, a draw.Keeping the direction of the wind in mind, he would often swap the ends of his fast bowlers to allow them a fair crack with the wind behind them. There were even shorter bursts of three overs each, but nothing worked as both Mitchell and Phillips never looked to score, which wasn't even necessary, and were happy blocking anything thrown at them.Mitchell, in particular, was the glue that held the innings together and was unperturbed by the wicketkeeper standing up. This ploy aimed to deny him movement towards the bowler and force him to play from the crease. The right-hander, however, trusted his defence and blunted the attack with 186-ball 49. In-form Phillips played a different role; batting time and not scoring boundaries were the need of the hour, and he did exactly what the team required. Faced 126 deliveries for his 26.As far as India are concerned, Prasidh Krishna, who received a lot of flak for his control in the first innings, was on the money in the second innings. The lanky seamer maintained consistent lines and lengths and also overtook Jasprit Bumrah's eight maidens by recording ten in his 19-over spell. India could have tried him with the second new ball instead of Akash Deep, as the Karnataka fast bowler was enjoying good rhythm and looked much better than his 26-100-1 in the first innings.The focus now shifts to Christchurch, where the two teams will lock horns for the second Test starting November 27. Crucial WTC points are up for grabs, and it will be a winner-takes-all scenario in the final game of India's long tour.720/9 declared;368 and 239/5 in 120 overs (Devon Conway 65, Daryl Mitchell 49 not out, Glenn Phillips 26 not out). Match drawn.
Article Summary: India took five wickets in their first innings using just 28.2 overs. They needed the same number of wickets to force a result in the second innings. Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips combined and were rock solid during their 63-run stand. The focus now shifts to Christchurch, where the two teams will lock horns for the second Test starting November 27.

India's chances of reaching the 2027 World Test Championship (WTC) final have taken a major hit after their opening Test against New Zealand ended in a draw at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Monday.India needed six wins from their remaining seven matches to stay on course for the summit clash. However, the drawn Test has made their task even tougher as they look to secure a place in the top two.Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips frustrated the Indian bowlers with a determined batting display on the final day. New Zealand, resuming at 119/2 and still 233 runs behind India's first-innings total, finished on 239/5 after batting for 120 overs to save the Test.India managed to take only three wickets on the final day after New Zealand resumed their innings with eight wickets in hand.Devon Conway (65) and Rachin Ravindra (37) were dismissed in the morning session, with Washington Sundar and Prasidh Krishna providing the breakthroughs. Anshul Kamboj then removed Tom Blundell (15 off 54 balls), but India struggled to make further inroads.A fielding error by Akash Deep also proved costly as he failed to collect the ball cleanly and missed a run-out opportunity against Mitchell.Mitchell made the most of the reprieve, remaining unbeaten on 49 off 186 balls. First-innings centurion Phillips also held his ground, scoring an unbeaten 26 off 126 deliveries. The pair faced 259 balls together to ensure New Zealand finished at 239/5 in 120 overs.Earlier, India had declared their first innings at 702/9 after dismissing New Zealand for 368.India's route to the 2027 WTC final has become difficult after the draw against New Zealand. They will need a strong finish in their remaining matches to stay in contention for a top-two position.Before the Wellington Test, India needed six wins from seven matches to have a realistic chance of reaching the final. The drawn result has reduced their room for error further.The draw has reduced India's points percentage (PCT) from 51.52 to 50.00. They remain fourth in the WTC 2025-27 standings but have lost valuable ground in the race for the final.South Africa continue to lead the table with a PCT of 75 after winning six of their eight Tests. Australia are second with 69.23, while New Zealand have moved to third with 66.67.

Article Title: Gagan Narang emerges frontrunner for IOA president’s post
Article Text:
Gagan Narang (Image credit: Olympics.com)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: With the nomination process for the Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) 2026-2030 elections beginning on Sunday, the race for key positions in the country's premier sports body has gathered momentum, with Gagan Narang emerging as a likely consensus candidate for the president's post from the govt side, sources tracking developments told TOI.Narang, the incumbent vice-president and an Olympic medallist, has made a strong pitch for himself in recent days, holding meetings with influential people in political circles as the govt looks to shape the IOA leadership for the next four years. Sources indicated that Narang is almost certain to file his nomination and has emerged as the preferred candidate.The incumbent president P T Usha, who has found her way back into the electoral race after securing nomination as the female representative from the Ice Hockey Association of India (IHAI), is likely to contest against Narang, her camp has indicated.However, the National Sports Federations (NSFs), which account for 60 votes in the electoral college, are still weighing their options. While a section is believed to be considering backing a govt-supported candidate, others are exploring the possibility of rallying behind Usha to trump Narang or fielding their own candidate to avoid splitting votes.Former Athletics Federation of India (AFI) chief Adille Sumariwalla, former IOA secretary general Rajeev Mehta and former Delhi state BJP president and Archery Association of India (AAI) secretary general Virender Sachdeva are among the names being discussed.Sachdeva has emerged as a possible dark horse in the presidential race. With his political connections and longstanding association with sports administration, he is believed to enjoy acceptability among both political circles and several NSFs, making him a potential consensus choice if the race takes an unexpected turn, sources said.The elections also assume significance with Ahmedabad set to host the 2030 CWG and India's ambitious Olympic bid for 2036 gaining traction. Gujarat-based administrators Chintan Parikh, Ajay H Patel and Udit Sheth are likely to secure key positions in the incoming executive council (EC), as TOI has previously reported.The nomination process will run until Nov 24, after which returning officer Sanjay K Srivastava is expected to finalise the candidates.Meanwhile, it's been learnt the Boxing Federation of India (BFI) has failed to secure voting rights. The federation, embroiled in internal disputes and recognition issues, was excluded from the electoral college for IOA polls. The Delhi High Court had referred BFI's plea for voting rights to the returning officer for a hearing. However, sources said the federation was not granted relief.The Indian Golf Union's (IGU) rival factions have also approached Srivastava following the high court's directive for a hearing on Monday. The Table Tennis Federation of India, meanwhile, is unlikely to get relief as its suspension-related matter remains before the court. The two federations were also excluded from the electoral college because of their internal disputes.
Article Summary: The nomination process for the Indian Olympic Association's (IOA) 2026-2030 elections begins on Sunday. Gagan Narang has emerged as a likely consensus candidate for the president's post from the govt side. The Boxing Federation of India (BFI) has failed to secure voting rights.

Article Title: Made tactical mistakes, erred, but risks are must for India to progress: Jamil
Article Text:
Khalid Jamil has handed debuts to 18 players in his first year in-charge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Panaji: The stats don’t lie.Khalid Jamil has been in this business for over 15 years and needs no reminding that a coach gets judged by the results he obtains. His record with the national team isn’t encouraging. Two wins from 17 matches, five draws, for a 12% winning rate and 0.7 points per match.Jamil’s first win came in Jamil’s first game as national team coach, against Tajikistan. It was a wonderful start but 2026 saw the team notch just one win, in an inconsequential tie against lower-ranked Hong Kong.“As a coach, I’ve erred, made mistakes tactically, but I’ve taken risks too which were a must at this stage,” the India coach told TOI after the conclusion of the two international friendlies in New Zealand last week. “For example, I had two choices: play these friendlies against New Zealand, a World Cup team, or go to SAFF Championship, where India are the highest ranked (team). If I wanted to play it safe, I could have gone with the team to Bangladesh and improved the (winning) statistics. ”India have now lost four matches in a row, all against teams that featured at the last FIFA World Cup . Jamil’s side conceded 19 goals in five friendlies during the last two windows and scored twice, which included an encouraging 1-1 draw against Panama.“We were good against Panama, played brilliantly, could have even won. We dominated. Everyone was praising us. Now, everyone is saying we are miserable. The criticism is not good for the players. I’ve told them to stay strong mentally since they can get affected by all this negativity,” said Jamil.The coach himself has not been spared. He says he can handle the heat, though “criticism on social media based on religion is not good.” His selection policy is straightforward: “everybody is the same for me; perform and get into the team.”Since being appointed in August 2025, Jamil, 49, has handed debuts to 18 players, the most by any national team coach in his first year in-charge. Yet, despite the constant chopping and changing, India still does not wear a settled look. In fact, against New Zealand he fielded Ashique Kuruniyan, a winger, in midfield, while the position of centre-backs was also changed.“It’s not as if I took the centre-backs and played them as forwards,” shot back Jamil.“Ashique was needed in midfield because of his physicality. If you see the second half against New Zealand (which ended goalless), we played well. The best part is that we had five debutants in that half and I was impressed with the players. Hrithik (Tiwari) in goal, Tomba (Singh), (Lalrinliana) Hnamte, David (Lalhlansanga), (Muhammad) Suhail too.”Jamil feels India’s performances have to be seen from a different lens. Clubs refusing to release players, injuries to regulars (Anwar, Apuia, Sahal for NZ friendlies), different time zones, hectic travel and limited training sessions.“You cannot go into games blindly (without preparations). New Zealand was a big lesson for us,” said Jamil. “Without preparations, it’s not easy to play. Yes, it’s true that I have tried many players, made changes, experimented, because I want to find the best team. I accept the results were not good. But without risks (of playing much higher-ranked opponents), we cannot improve.“You have to be patient. You have to trust. I am not someone who will put his hands up (and quit). I will fight, 100%, for the country. I will complete the job.”Jamil signed a two-year contract in August last year with an assurance that he will have an uninterrupted run.
Article Summary: Khalid Jamil has won just two of 17 matches in charge of India. The 49-year-old has handed debuts to 18 players in his first year in-charge. India have now lost four matches in a row, all against teams that featured at the last FIFA World Cup.

Article Title: Gukesh has the crown, Sindarov has the momentum: A clash of two journeys
Article Text:
Javokhir Sindarov and Gukesh Dommaraju (Image credit: X)

KOLKATA: As a child, Gukesh Dommaraju would often scribble on the walls of his room. His wish was simple: “I want to be the youngest world champion.” At 18, he turned that childhood dream into reality, beating China’s Ding Liren in the World Chess Championship final in Singapore in 2024.Two years on, 20-year-old Gukesh faces a very different challenge. Having gone from being a young challenger taking on a vastly more experienced opponent to a reigning champion defending his crown, he must now contend with a rival his own age — Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov — in the 2026 World Chess Championship final in Geneva, Switzerland, from Tuesday onwards.The past two years have taken the world’s fourthyoungest (Gukesh) and sixth-youngest (Sindarov) Grandmasters in opposite directions. Gukesh has struggled to build on his World Championship triumph and is yet to win a tournament since that victory, while his rating has slipped from 2794 in Oct 2024 to 2703 in Sept 2026. Sindarov, by contrast, has surged, winning the 2025 World Cup and the 2026 Candidates Tournament to reach career-best marks in both rating and world ranking.When Gukesh challenged Ding in 2024, he was rated 55 points higher than the defending champion.This time, he starts as the lowest-ranked reigning champ in World Championship history at World No. 26. Sindarov, meanwhile, enjoys a 72-point rating advantage and a 22-place lead in the Nov FIDE rankings.The Uzbek’s coach, too, has noticed a change in his ward’s demeanour. Roman Vidonyak now describes Sindarov as a “predator”, suggesting that he is increasingly turning into a hunter on the board.Yet Gukesh’s recent slump appears less about his chess than about handling the weight of the title. He showed remarkable composure at the Chess Olympiad in Samarkand this year, willingly dropping to Board 4. Still, costly slips from advantageous positions — against Nodirbek Abdusattorov at the Prague Masters; and Arjun Erigaisi and M Pranesh at the Chennai Grand Masters — have exposed Gukesh’ recent vulnerabilities.Hogging the limelight so young carries its own burden, and the pressure has begun to tell. “Obviously there’s a lot of pressure, that I’m dealing with and I’ve not found the right way to maybe handle it yet,” Gukesh had admitted in a recent interaction.Playing away from home in Geneva could offer a welcome buffer from the outside noise and allow Gukesh to rediscover the freedom with which he played his way to the world title in 2024.One-time reigning champ vs first-time challengerlTigran Petrosian vs Boris Spassky (1966): Petrosian (age: 36) edged fellow Soviet GM Spassky (29) 12.5–11.5 to keep the crown.lDing Liren vs D Gukesh (2024): Indian challenger Gukesh (18) upset Chinese GM Ding (32) 7.5–6.5.

Article Title: ILT20: Chris Jordan, Zahoor Khan star as MI Emirates beat Desert Vipers by 52 runs in opener
Article Text:
Image credit: ILT20

Perera, Waseem give MI Emirates a flying start

Jordan, Zahoor lead Vipers' collapse

Perera, Shadab reflect on the match

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Brief scores

MI Emirates began their ILT20 Season 5 campaign with a convincing 52-run win over defending champions Desert Vipers at the Dubai International Stadium on Saturday.The victory was special for MI Emirates as they avenged their defeat to the Vipers in last season's final. After being asked to bat, MI Emirates posted 174/8 in 20 overs, thanks to Kusal Perera 's 58 and Muhammad Waseem's 41. The opening pair added 94 runs to give their team a strong start.In reply, the Desert Vipers were bowled out for 122 in 19.1 overs. Chris Jordan led the bowling attack with four wickets for 19 runs, while Zahoor Khan picked up three wickets for just 13 runs.Joe Clarke was the top scorer for the Vipers with 35 off 28 balls, but the defending champions could not build partnerships as wickets kept falling.MI Emirates got off to an aggressive start, with Perera and Waseem putting pressure on the Vipers' bowlers from the beginning.The opening pair added 94 runs in 9.5 overs. They scored 33 runs in the first three overs, including 17 runs off David Payne's bowling. The Vipers managed to slow things down towards the end of the powerplay, with MI Emirates reaching 54 without losing a wicket.Naseem Shah finally broke the partnership in the 10th over when Waseem edged a delivery to wicketkeeper Andries Gous. Waseem scored 41 off 30 balls.Perera continued to score freely and completed his half-century in 34 balls with a boundary off Mujeeb Ur Rahman.He was dismissed for 58 in the 14th over after mistiming a shot off Payne, with Gous taking the catch.The Vipers then picked up wickets at regular intervals. Khuzaima Tanveer dismissed Sherfane Rutherford (5) with the help of a brilliant catch from Tom Curran.Nicholas Pooran added 32 off 19 balls before mistiming a shot off Mujeeb and getting caught by Payne.Captain Shadab Khan dismissed Sanjay Krishnamurthi (2), while Tanveer took a return catch to remove Romario Shepherd (3). Naseem then dismissed Kieron Pollard (15) in the final over as MI Emirates finished with 174/8.Chasing 175, the Desert Vipers lost Fakhar Zaman (12) in the fifth over when he was caught by Gudakesh Motie off Zahoor Khan.MI Emirates kept the scoring under control, restricting the Vipers to 43/1 at the end of the powerplay.Clarke tried to keep the chase alive with 35 off 28 balls, including five boundaries. However, Motie dismissed him in the 11th over.Zahoor then picked up his second wicket by removing Gous (15 off 22 balls). Rashid Khan added to the Vipers' problems by dismissing captain Shadab (6) in the 14th over.The dismissal of Shadab started a major collapse. Jordan removed Nangeyalia Kharoti (1) and Shimron Hetmyer (21), while Tanveer (1) also fell in the same over. Jordan picked up two of those three wickets.Gudakesh Motie then dismissed Tom Curran (3), who was caught brilliantly by Kieron Pollard. The Vipers were reduced to 109/8 in the 17th over.Jordan claimed his fourth wicket by dismissing Vriitya Aravind (21), while Zahoor completed his three-wicket haul by removing Naseem Shah (2). The Vipers were bowled out for 122 in 19.1 overs, handing MI Emirates a comfortable victory.Kusal Perera was named Player of the Match for his match-winning 58. He said making the most of the powerplay was the plan and spoke about the work he had put into his batting."The plan was simple: make the most of the powerplay. I got a bit lucky off the first ball, and after that I backed my strengths whenever the ball was in my areas. I've been working on this for the last two to three years. The pressure is high in leagues, but we try to express ourselves, and the management encourages us to play that way."Desert Vipers captain Shadab Khan admitted that his team gave away too many runs in the first 10 overs. However, he felt the bowling improved later in the innings."We were too loose in the first 10 overs and gave away too many runs, but we recovered well as a group. Our bowling was better in the second half, and the pitch seemed to hold up a lot in the second innings. We all know how good Naseem is, and he has been showing that quality all year."MI Emirates: 174/8 in 20 overs (Kusal Perera 58, Muhammad Waseem 41, Nicholas Pooran 32; Naseem Shah 2/24, Khuzaima Tanveer 2/40)Desert Vipers: 122 all out in 19.1 overs (Joe Clarke 35, Shimron Hetmyer 21, Vriitya Aravind 21; Chris Jordan 4/19, Zahoor Khan 3/13)Result: MI Emirates won by 52 runsPlayer of the Match: Kusal Perera
Article Summary: MI Emirates beat defending champions Desert Vipers by 52 runs in Dubai. MI Emirates posted 174/8 in 20 overs, thanks to Kusal Perera's 58. The Vipers were bowled out for 122 in 19.1 overs. Chris Jordan led the bowling attack with four wickets for 19 runs.

Article Title: Rawalpindi Test: Pakistan end two-year drought as Sri Lanka suffer historic low with four straight away series defeats
Article Text:
Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by 8 wickets in the Pawalpindi Test. (Pic credit: SLC)

Sri Lanka's overseas struggles deepen

Babar praises youngsters as Mendis looks ahead

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A new-look Pakistan side ended a two-year wait for a Test series triumph, overpowering Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the second Test in Rawalpindi on Friday to clinch the two-match series 1-0. The defeat extended Sri Lanka's miserable overseas run, leaving them with four successive away Test series losses and a calendar year without a single Test victory for the first time since 1997.Chasing a modest target after restricting Sri Lanka to 316 in their second innings, Pakistan raced to 90/2 in just 13 overs during the first session on Day 4. Aamer Jamal provided the finishing flourish with an unbeaten 34 off 22 balls, smashing five fours and a six, while Azan Awais remained not out on 32.The victory was Pakistan's first Test series win since beating England at home in October 2024. It was also only their third win in 11 matches in the current World Test Championship cycle.Pakistan captain Babar Azam was particularly pleased with the way his relatively inexperienced side responded to the challenge."Very satisfying, the way the team performed. We had a young team, many players grabbed their opportunities.The environment in the dressing room is very positive, we just need to stay stable and focus on the game. All the players gave 100% to their roles and that was nice to see," Babar said.The series defeat added another unwanted chapter to Sri Lanka's recent Test record. Their last overseas series victory came against Bangladesh in March 2024, and they have now lost four consecutive away series.The Islanders will also finish 2026 without a Test victory for the first time since 1997. Pakistan, meanwhile, have won three of their last four Test series against Sri Lanka, whose previous series triumph over Pakistan came in September 2017.Sri Lanka's troubles in Rawalpindi began in the first innings when Pakistan's seamers bowled them out for just 98 inside the first two sessions on the opening day. The visitors conceded a massive 227-run first-innings lead, leaving themselves with a mountain to climb.They showed greater resistance in the second innings, with Milan Rathnayake remaining unbeaten on 66 to help extend the contest. However, Mohammad Abbas, who claimed 3/55 in the innings, ended the resistance by trapping Asitha Fernando lbw in his first over on Friday.Abbas, who was named both Player of the Match and Player of the Series, said his performance had been overdue."The performance was due, I spoke before the series and the challenges before it, still have to take a 5-wicket haul, hopefully I will do it. I assess the conditions, make sure that my economy is low and it helps the other bowlers as well. I only advised them to hit the areas well, Saqib became unfit unfortunately, that made my responsibility more," he said.Pakistan's victory was particularly encouraging given the number of fresh faces in the squad, with four players making their debuts during the series. Babar singled out wicketkeeper-batter Ghazi for making the most of his opportunities and also credited fast bowler Razaullah's pace and first-innings contribution."If you have a bowler who can bowl at 145 kmph, it gives you confidence. His spell in the first innings was vital and that was one of the main reasons for our series win today," Babar said.Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis acknowledged that his side's poor first-innings batting had proved costly."Honestly, we didn't bat well in the first innings, including me. I got out at a crucial time. We bowled well and batted well in the 2nd innings. Bowling wise, I thought we hit the areas well," Mendis said.He also thanked Pakistan for hosting the team during a tour that included a 2-1 T20I series defeat and a loss in the ODI tri-series final."We've stayed here for more than one month, we enjoyed Pakistan and have had positives in both Tests. The fast bowlers bowled well and I'm happy with the improvement. Looking forward to the tour of New Zealand. Hopefully, I will be back here in the PSL or some other tournament. I thank Pakistan for hosting us, we enjoyed our stay here," he added.
Article Summary: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the second Test in Rawalpindi. Pakistan won the two-match series 1-0 to claim their first Test series win since beating England in October 2024. Sri Lanka have now lost four consecutive away Test series.

Article Title: Mohammed Siraj snub under scanner as India pacers struggle! Kotak defends team selection after New Zealand fightback in 1st Test
Article Text:
Mohammed Siraj and Sitanshu Kotak

Kotak explains why Siraj was left out

'Prasidh is an attacking bowler'

NEW DELHI: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defended the decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand, insisting that the selectors and team management had picked the best possible combination despite the pacer's omission coming under scrutiny after a difficult opening day for India's bowling attack at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday.With Jasprit Bumrah doing most of the damage, India's other pace options struggled to make an impact as New Zealand recovered from 70/5 to reach 243/5 at stumps. Henry Nicholls remained unbeaten on 113, while Glenn Phillips was six runs short of a century at 94 not out, the pair putting together an unbroken 173-run stand for the sixth wicket.Siraj's absence was particularly noticeable as Anshul Kamboj, playing in his place, managed just one wicket for 57 runs in 18 overs. Prasidh Krishna went wicketless, conceding 58 runs in 16 overs, while Akash Deep returned figures of 1/33. Bumrah, meanwhile, finished with 3/52 from 17 overs.Asked about Siraj's omission at the post-day press conference, Kotak backed the selection call and said the team management had considered the conditions and opposition while settling on its best XI."I think at a time they pick the team, they think about the best XI, and that’s what played. Nothing wrong with Siraj, they thought of the best possible XI and played.Sri Lanka was different conditions. Not wrong decision to drop Siraj," Kotak said.He also explained the thinking behind India's bowling combination, pointing to the different skills offered by the pace attack and the decision to include Washington Sundar because New Zealand had four left-handers in their XI."On current attack: Two bowlers swing the ball well and two seam the ball well. And have pace. When you pick XI, you think about all days. Picked Washi because of four left-handers in opposition XI," he added.The decision, however, came under the spotlight as Bumrah repeatedly troubled the New Zealand batters while the other Indian bowlers struggled to maintain pressure after the new ball lost its shine.Kotak also defended Prasidh, whose expensive spell included several boundary-scoring deliveries, saying the Karnataka pacer was an attacking option who could be expensive while searching for wickets."Prasidh is an attacking bowler and he can go for runs. People like it when he picks wickets, and they don’t when they go for runs," Kotak said.India had made an impressive start after winning the toss, with Bumrah removing Tom Latham, Devon Conway and Daryl Mitchell before dismissing Tom Blundell to reduce the hosts to 70/5. Kamboj also struck early, but Nicholls and Phillips turned the contest around with a patient yet increasingly assured partnership.Kotak felt India had an opportunity to make further inroads, particularly with a chance to dismiss Nicholls going down."The pitch helped with the new ball, the weather was good and sunny so it dried out. We should have taken that catch, Rishabh Pant went for the catch but it was close to Devdutt Padikkal," he said.Nicholls eventually reached his 12th Test century, while Phillips continued to counter-attack as India's bowling attack lost its early bite. Bumrah was the only bowler who consistently threatened, leaving India with plenty to ponder after surrendering control of a day that had begun so promisingly.
Article Summary: India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak defends decision to leave Mohammed Siraj out of the playing XI for the first Test against New Zealand. Kotak says selectors and team management had picked the best possible combination despite Siraj's omission. Jasprit Bumrah was the only bowler who consistently threatened New Zealand's batting line-up.

Article Title: India clinch historic lawn bowls series in New Zealand
Article Text:
(From left) Dinesh Kumar, Reshma Kumari, Pinki Singh and Sunil Bahadur after winning the trophy in Auckland on Wednesday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India completed a remarkable turnaround to clinch the three-match lawn bowls series against New Zealand with a 3-2 victory in the deciding test at Royal Oak Bowls in Auckland on Wednesday.Having lost the opening test before levelling the series with a comeback win on Tuesday, the Indian team produced another composed performance to seal the trophy on New Zealand soil.The experienced Jharkhand duo of Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur gave India a winning start, defeating their New Zealand opponents 9-7 in the men’s pairs. New Zealand hit back in the women’s pairs, where Reshma Kumari and Pinki Singh went down 2-5.India regained the advantage in the mixed fours as the quartet grabbed a crucial 7-5 victory. The visitors then sealed the overall test by winning the first mixed pairs contest 5-2. Although New Zealand claimed the second mixed pairs match 7-4, India had already secured an unassailable lead and with it the test and the series.The triumph completed a stunning recovery after India lost the opening test and found themselves adapting to unfamiliar conditions in Auckland. According to Dinesh, belief in their own abilities proved crucial to the turnaround.“We know that if we play our natural game, we can challenge any team in the world. We showed that here. We kept reminding each other to play our best and leave everything on the green. Everyone gave their all, and we achieved our goal,” he said on Wednesday.For Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki, the key to India’s revival lay in the unity shown by the four-member contingent. “The best thing was our unity. None of us made excuses about being tired, lacking sleep or facing difficult conditions. All four of us played as one team. We fought together, came back together and eventually won the series together,” Pinki said.Sunil, meanwhile, underlined the significance of winning the trophy away from home.“The biggest satisfaction comes from winning on New Zealand’s home turf. Winning in India would have been special, but coming here, competing in their conditions and taking the trophy back home makes the achievement even more meaningful,” he said.The series victory provides another significant boost for Indian lawn bowls in what has already been a successful year for the sport and will serve as a confidence booster ahead of upcoming international competitions, including the World Championships.
Article Summary: India complete remarkable turnaround to clinch three-match lawn bowls series against New Zealand with a 3-2 victory in the deciding test at Royal Oak Bowls in Auckland on Wednesday. The triumph completed a stunning recovery after India lost the opening test and found themselves adapting to unfamiliar conditions in Auckland.

Article Title: Venugopal Rao: 'Built a cricket ecosystem from scratch, now ready for the next chapter'
Article Text:
Venugopal Rao, Delhi Capitals former director of cricket. speaks to Sameer Rizvi after a net session during the IPL 2025 at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in New Delhi. (ANI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Former India cricketer Venugopal Rao says he is "happy" and "content" when asked what's next for him after ending his four-and-a-half-year association with GMR Group 's cricket franchises, where he served as Director of Cricket."I am in Hyderabad, enjoying my time away from cricket. Now I'm taking some time out to be with my family. My kids have also been asking for my time, so that's important," Rao tells TimesofIndia.com.The 44-year-old has been the architect of the GMR Group's cricketing operations across the globe. He played a pivotal role in guiding Dubai Capitals to the ILT20 title in 2025 and was appointed Delhi Capitals' Director of Cricket for the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons. He also joined Seattle Orcas as General Manager of Cricket Operations and has helped steady the ship at Southern Brave in The Hundred, a franchise in which the GMR Group has invested heavily."For four-and-a-half years, I was involved day in and day out, setting up the entire system. When I came in, nothing was in place. I built the whole cricket ecosystem, brought people in, and they did well," he says."But I will definitely get involved with teams and do something in cricket again. I can't keep myself away from the game for too long. For the next four or five months, I'll take some time and see what happens. I'm looking forward to opportunities and will see where things go," adds Rao, a veteran of 121 first-class matches.Under Venugopal Rao and head coach Hemang Badani, the Delhi-based franchise finished fifth and sixth in IPL 2025 and 2026, respectively. Sourav Ganguly has now been appointed as Delhi Capitals' head coach ahead of IPL 2027. The move follows the agreement reached between DC co-owners GMR Sports India Pvt Ltd and JSW Sports, under which the two partners would alternate control of the franchise's operations in two-year cycles.“When you look back at our first season (IPL 2025), especially the two games against Mumbai Indians, one at home and one away, I think we could have won both. In the first game in Delhi, we had four or five run-outs, which cost us the match. Karun played a superb knock, and we could have chased the target comfortably. Even in the Mumbai game, we had four or five run-outs, which again cost us," Rao reflects."In the Mumbai game, Axar Patel missed out due to illness. If you look at the surface, it was turning, and Mitchell Santner was a crucial bowler for them who picked up an important wicket. Axar was a big miss for us, not just with the ball but also while batting. As a left-hander, he would have been better equipped to tackle left-arm spin."Those were the two games in our first season that we missed out on, and winning them could have helped us qualify for the knockouts."Rao feels that even in the second season, in 2026, they were in contention for the playoff spots and could have qualified with a bit of luck."Even in the second season, if you look back at the home game against Gujarat Titans, David Miller was on strike. We needed two runs off two balls, but we couldn't win the game. That was our biggest disappointment. A player like Miller should have finished that game," he says."There was also the game against Punjab in which we scored 265. A lot of people say we should have defended that total, but if you look at the circumstances, Lungi Ngidi got injured and had to go to the hospital. That cost us around four hours. At the same time, we dropped eight catches."Normally, if you score 265 and drop eight catches, it's difficult to defend that total. If we had won those two games, Gujarat would have finished in the top two. That's how the IPL works, and we had to accept it," he adds.On the debate over whether Axar Patel or KL Rahul should lead Delhi Capitals (DC), Rao believes the incoming leadership should be allowed to operate without interference.“Whoever takes over should be given a free hand. Whether it’s Axar or KL, both have played at this level and understand the game. I have always believed in giving people freedom. Mistakes can happen, but your intentions should be good. If they are, you should have the clarity and freedom to take decisions," he says.Rao cites KL Rahul's turnaround as an example. After a slow start in IPL 2024, Rahul finished as the franchise's leading run-scorer, amassing 539 runs that season and 593 in IPL 2025."We backed KL Rahul and gave him a particular role. From the first season to the second, we worked on building his confidence. We told him he would have our support, and that was important. He delivered. He told us that if we backed him, he would deliver the results, and he did," he says.Rao also stressed that backing the coaching staff and management is central to building a successful franchise. Citing Chennai Super Kings' turnaround after a difficult 2020 season and RCB's consistency in reaching the playoffs before winning the title in 2025, he said teams needed to trust their cricketing personnel and allow them to work."The difference between teams that win championships and those that don't is often the support staff, the processes and the freedom given to people. Miracles may happen occasionally, but consistency is what helps teams win trophies and matches. Look at teams like CSK, Mumbai Indians and Kolkata Knight Riders. When the management gives people a free hand, it makes a difference."I still remember Chennai Super Kings having a difficult season in 2020. They didn't finish in the top four, but from what I heard from MS Dhoni, he maintained the same atmosphere in the dressing room and didn't allow outside interference. The following season, they won the trophy."You can see something similar with Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB). The hard work over three years helped them consistently qualify for the playoffs. When I spoke to Faf du Plessis, who was with us at DC, he told me that the cricketing decisions were largely left to the cricketers.The management was involved, but the cricketing people had the freedom to do their job."In franchise cricket, you often see the difference when the people responsible for cricket are allowed to take decisions. There is a lot of noise on social media, with people asking teams to change this or that. But if you keep interfering, the franchise will always struggle to build consistency," he adds.
Article Summary: Former India cricketer Venugopal Rao says he is "happy" and "content" when asked what's next for him after ending his four-and-a-half-year association with GMR Group's cricket franchises. He played a pivotal role in guiding Dubai Capitals to the ILT20 title in 2025 and was appointed Delhi Capitals' Director of Cricket for the 2025 and 2026 IPL seasons. He also joined Seattle Orcas as General Manager of Cricket Operations.

Article Title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Tom Latham explains why New Zealand are 'happy' with Wellington draw despite India domination
Article Text:

Latham highlights importance of WTC points

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: New Zealand captain Tom Latham believes his team has earned a result that feels like a victory after managing to draw the first Test against India in Wellington on Monday. He said the draw was especially satisfying considering the difficult positions New Zealand found themselves in during the match.India declared their first innings at 720/9 but fell five wickets short of victory after Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips put up a strong fight on the final day. The pair batted patiently for almost two sessions to keep India from taking the remaining wickets.The match going into the fifth day had looked unlikely after India reduced New Zealand to 70/5 shortly after lunch on the opening day. However, the pitch became easier for batting, allowing the hosts to recover and score 368 in their first innings."I guess that's one that we've probably got away with," Latham told reporters at Basin Reserve."Looking at the position we were in on day one, I think the amount of pressure that we were put under to then be in a position where we got 360 or 370... we were certainly pretty happy (with that)."Heading into the third innings, where there's only a couple of results at play, I think (it's great) the way those guys were able to apply themselves and stick to their plans for a long period of time, and ultimately get the draw."Latham, who was dismissed for ducks in both innings by Jasprit Bumrah in the first over each time, said the draw could prove important in New Zealand's bid to reach the World Test Championship (WTC) final.New Zealand were at the top of the WTC standings when the Test began last week but were overtaken by defending champions South Africa. Monday's draw will see them drop another place to third, behind Australia.However, with the second Test against India in Christchurch still to come, followed by a tour of Australia and a home series against Sri Lanka, Latham believes his team has enough matches left to fight for one of the two places in the WTC final at The Oval in June."Draws become important as well," added the opener, who helped New Zealand beat India in 2021 to win the first WTC final."It's not necessarily over one series that you've got to play well. It's over a two-year period and it depends on how many games you've got."Obviously, we've got more games left than most teams... (and) hopefully, we'll give ourselves a chance throughout the next couple of months to be in that position."
Article Summary: New Zealand captain Tom Latham believes his team earned a result that feels like a victory. New Zealand managed to draw the first Test against India in Wellington on Monday. Latham said the draw could prove important in New Zealand's bid to reach the World Test Championship final.

NEW DELHI: Prithvi Shaw has hit back at former cricketer Yograj Singh over his remarks about the batter's career and personal life. He also compared the Indian batter's situation with that of former India cricketer Vinod Kambli "Why did Prithvi Shaw go downhill? It happened with Vinod Kambli before him. Then the girl he was with left him, and no one offered him cigarettes and alcohol. The same happened with Shaw. When you go to parties, womanise, drink, and are in bad company, the same will happen to you as happened to them," he added.Shaw responded to Yograj's comments through a detailed Instagram statement.The batter said he had no issues with his past but would not accept attempts to target him or spread false claims about his personal life."My past is a part of my life, and I have absolutely nothing to hide or be ashamed of. However, I will not tolerate individuals deliberately using my name, my personal life, or my past to spread negativity, create unnecessary controversy, damage my reputation, or gain publicity and attention at my expense. There is a clear difference between expressing an opinion and deliberately targeting someone with false, misleading, defamatory, or malicious content. Let this be a clear and final warning: Any individual or platform engaging in such activities may face appropriate legal action," Shaw said.The batter also said he was ready to take legal steps to protect his dignity, privacy and reputation. He made it clear that his silence should not be mistaken for weakness."I reserve the right to pursue all legal remedies available to protect my dignity, privacy, and reputation. My silence should never be mistaken for weakness. I choose to move forward with dignity, but I will not hesitate to stand up for myself," he added.Shaw last represented India in 2021. Article Title: When did India last play back-to-back drawn Tests before Wellington and Colombo?

Second consecutive draw for India

India's bowlers put in a long effort on the final day of the first Test against New Zealand, but the pitch at the Basin Reserve offered little help as the hosts held on for a draw in Wellington on Monday. Daryl Mitchell and Glenn Phillips batted through the final session to ensure New Zealand finished their second innings at 239/5 before the two captains agreed to shake hands.India had started the day hoping to take eight wickets, with New Zealand resuming at 119/2. However, Mitchell remained unbeaten on 49 off 187 balls, while Phillips made 26 not out off 126 deliveries as the hosts resisted India's attack.The result was only the second drawn Test at the Basin Reserve in 15 matches since 2015. The other came in December 2018, when Sri Lanka, after conceding a 296-run first-innings lead, finished at 287/3 in 115 overs in the third innings. They had been reduced to 13/3 in 6.2 overs before staging their fightback.The draw has also affected India's chances of qualifying for the World Test Championship final. New Zealand slipped from second to third with a points percentage of 66.67.South Africa continued to lead the table with 75 per cent, while Australia moved up to second place with 69.23 per cent.There was a strong breeze and some cloud cover throughout the day, but the pitch remained easy to bat on. The New Zealand batters were able to play their shots and defend without having to deal with uneven bounce. Mitchell and Phillips, both known for their white-ball batting, showed their defensive skills as India captain Shubman Gill kept rotating his bowlers but could not find a way through.This was India's second consecutive drawn Test and further affected their chances of reaching the World Test Championship final. Earlier in August, India had drawn the second Test against Sri Lanka at the SSC in Colombo after enforcing the follow-on.The last time India had played two or more consecutive drawn Tests was more than a decade ago. They had three draws in a row during the 2014-15 tour of Australia, against Australia in Melbourne and Sydney, followed by a draw against Bangladesh in June 2015.

Article Title: 'Edicts coming from above': MCC reacts to India's handshake boycott against Pakistan

The Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC), the custodian of cricket's laws, will not intervene in India's decision to avoid customary handshakes with Pakistan players, its head of cricket Fraser Stewart said on Sunday.The unofficial boycott began during the 2025 men's Asia Cup , held weeks after the Pahalgam terror attack . The practice has since extended across men's and women's cricket, different age groups and tournaments. Both teams also did not shake hands after Rising Stars Asia Cup match between India A and Pakistan A on Sunday, which Pakistan A won by 48 runs.While the MCC is responsible for the laws of cricket, handshakes are not covered by them. Stewart said the issue involved matters beyond the organisation's authority and that its focus remained on ensuring respect between players and match officials on the field.“There are certain instances that transcend cricket and come from a level that’s above my station to talk about geopolitical situations," Stewart said, as quoted by news agency PTI. “What we can control is that, on the field, the players respect each other, they respect the umpires, the authority of the umpires and the game."Stewart said he would like to see the practice return to normal but acknowledged that the MCC had little control over a decision linked to wider political issues.“That’s what we can control. If there are edicts coming from above about handshakes, that’s not something that MCC is able to control. We would like to see it, but we realise that there are bigger issues at play and that’s something that’s beyond anything we can control," he said.Stewart also spoke about the Sandpapergate controversy, which has returned to the spotlight following fresh revelations from Usman Khawaja, Chadd Sayers and Cameron Bancroft. He said the MCC would not comment on the claims or Cricket Australia's investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering incident.However, Stewart made it clear that using sandpaper on the ball was a violation of cricket's laws.“I think my line on that would be that, as far as the laws of cricket are concerned, using sandpaper on the ball is a clear breach of the law," Stewart said. “I don’t think anyone is doubting that it was the case. What goes on and who knew what, and making further allegations eight years later, that’s not really something for MCC to comment on."

Article Title: Best ever! From 14 medals to 114: How India achieved more with fewer athletes at the Asian Para Games
Article Text:
Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

From 14 medals to 114: India's remarkable rise

India's Asian Para Games record

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Smaller contingent, bigger return

Hangzhou vs Aichi-Nagoya

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Athletics powers India's medal surge

India's leading medal-winning sports in Asian Para Games 2026

Image credit: TimesofIndia.com

Multiple medallists underline India's depth

Paralympic progress provides the wider context

Fourth place sets a new benchmark

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

From 14 medals in 2010 to 114 in 2026, India’s remarkable rise continued in Aichi-Nagoya as a smaller contingent surpassed its previous best, achieved 30 gold medals and secured its highest-ever finish at the continental para-sport showpiece.India’s campaign at the Asian Para Games 2026 was a triumph that few would have predicted when the size of the contingent became known. With just 167 athletes travelling to Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, the prospect of repeating the 100-plus medal haul achieved at Hangzhou in 2023 appeared ambitious. The previous edition had seen India send more than 300 athletes to the competition, returning with a record 108 medals after subsequent revisions to the original tally.But the Indian contingent defied expectations, producing an even bigger return with significantly fewer athletes. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place, both the highest medal tally and the best finish in the country's history at the event.The numbers tell a compelling story of progress. India improved its medal tally for the fifth consecutive edition, added to its gold-medal record and finished ahead of South Korea, which had threatened to challenge its position in the final standings.More than the record itself, the achievement highlighted how far India's para-sport movement has travelled in 16 years — from a modest 14-medal return at the inaugural edition in 2010 to a fourth-place finish among Asia's leading para-sport nations.India's progress at the Asian Para Games has been steady, with each edition bringing a new high in the overall medal tally.At Guangzhou in 2010, India won 14 medals — one gold, four silver and nine bronze — to finish 15th. The 2014 edition in Incheon brought a substantial improvement, with the country collecting 33 medals, including three gold, but remaining 15th in the standings.The breakthrough arrived at Jakarta in 2018. India's medal tally rose to 72, comprising 15 gold, 24 silver and 33 bronze, while its position improved to ninth.Hangzhou in 2023 marked another major leap. India crossed the 100-medal barrier for the first time, initially returning with 111 medals before the tally was revised to 108 following a doping-related disqualification and a medal reallocation. The revised haul comprised 27 gold, 32 silver and 49 bronze, with India eventually classified sixth.Aichi-Nagoya extended that upward trajectory. India added six medals to its revised Hangzhou total, increased its gold-medal count from 27 to 30 and climbed two places to fourth.The numbers at a glance: India's medal tally increased more than eightfold between 2010 and 2026. Its gold-medal count grew from one to 30, while its position improved from 15th to fourth.The rise has not been limited to the overall tally. India has improved its standing in three successive editions since 2014, moving from 15th to ninth, then sixth and now fourth. The 2026 result represents the culmination of a sustained upward trend rather than an isolated breakthrough.The most striking feature of India's latest performance was the efficiency with which its athletes converted participation into medals.India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi-Nagoya. That was considerably fewer than the 309 athletes listed for the Hangzhou campaign in 2023, yet the team surpassed its previous best by six medals.The comparison is revealing. India sent approximately 46 per cent fewer athletes than it did to Hangzhou, but its medal tally increased by nearly six per cent. The gold-medal count rose by three, the silver tally by three, and the bronze count remained unchanged.On a simple medals-per-athlete measure, India's return increased from approximately 0.35 medals per athlete in Hangzhou to 0.68 in Aichi-Nagoya. This is an aggregate comparison, not an individual success rate, since athletes can win multiple medals and the number of events and opportunities varies across sports.Nevertheless, the figures underline the scale of the achievement. A smaller squad did not merely match the previous edition's success; it established a new benchmark for Indian para-sport.Para-athletics was the backbone of India's campaign, delivering 65 medals — 22 gold, 19 silver and 24 bronze. That represented nearly 57 per cent of the country's overall tally and made athletics the single biggest contributor to India's fourth-place finish.Para-badminton followed with 16 medals, including three gold, five silver and eight bronze. Together, athletics and badminton accounted for 81 medals, more than 70 per cent of India's total.Swimming contributed 11 medals, comprising three silver and eight bronze. Archery added six medals, including three gold and three silver, while shooting produced five, with two gold, two silver and one bronze.Athletics' contribution also illustrates how India's progress has accelerated. At Hangzhou, para-athletics produced 52 medals, including 16 gold, 17 silver and 19 bronze. In Aichi-Nagoya, the discipline's haul rose to 65, with six additional gold medals.Badminton's contribution was different. India won 21 medals in the sport at Hangzhou, including four gold, but finished with 16 in 2026. Instead, the substantial gains in athletics and the contributions from other sports helped compensate for the decline in badminton medals.That distinction matters: the record haul reflects both the strength of India's established medal-winning disciplines and the need to broaden its success across events in future editions.India's record was supported by athletes who delivered more than once during the competition. A total of 26 Indian athletes won multiple medals, while six athletes collected multiple gold medals, demonstrating the importance of individual excellence in a campaign involving 11 sports.Archer Sheetal Devi was among the standout performers, winning two gold medals and a silver. Her two golds came in the mixed compound and individual compound events, while the silver added to her three-medal haul.Athletics provided several other multiple gold medallists. Dilip Gavit, Nishad Kumar, Pranav Soorma and Simran Sharma each won two gold medals, while shooting contributed through Mona Agarwal, who also secured two golds.Four athletes finished with three medals apiece: Sheetal Devi in archery, Thulasimathi Murugesan in badminton, Ravi Budigina in swimming and Himanshu Nandal in swimming. Their performances illustrated how athletes winning across multiple events can make a significant difference to a country's final tally.The figures also invite comparison with Hangzhou, where 25 Indian athletes won multiple medals. The increase to 26 in 2026 was modest, but the overall tally improved despite a much smaller contingent. The result points to a campaign in which medal-winning performances were concentrated among a relatively small squad.India's rise at the Asian Para Games has coincided with a significant improvement at the Paralympics, strengthening the country's standing in international para-sport.At Rio 2016, India won four medals and finished 43rd. Tokyo 2020 marked a breakthrough, with 19 medals — five gold, eight silver and six bronze — lifting India to 24th. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best Paralympic haul of 29 medals, comprising seven gold, nine silver and 13 bronze, to finish 18th.The progression at the Paralympics mirrors the broader trend at the Asian Para Games: larger medal returns, more gold medals and improvements in the standings.India's able-bodied contingent had also finished fourth at the 2026 Asian Games, although its 85-medal tally was below the 106 medals achieved at Hangzhou in 2023. The para contingent's performance offered a contrasting story of growth, with its medal count rising and its position improving.China dominated Aichi-Nagoya, finishing with 435 medals, including 207 gold. Hosts Japan were second with 186 medals, while Uzbekistan finished third with 145. India placed fourth with 114, ahead of South Korea, which collected 100 medals, including 29 gold.India's final position was not guaranteed until the closing stages. South Korea remained within reach, but its final-day return of one gold and two silver left it one gold behind India. The Indian contingent held on to fourth place with 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze.The gap to third-placed Uzbekistan shows that further progress will require India to expand its medal-winning strength across disciplines. Yet the immediate achievement is significant: India has moved from 15th at the first two editions to fourth, while increasing its tally at every successive Games.The challenge now is to sustain that momentum, build a deeper pool of competitive athletes and reduce dependence on a handful of disciplines.For a contingent of just 167 athletes, 114 medals represent more than a record. They mark the latest step in a 16-year transformation of Indian para-sport — one that began with 14 medals in Guangzhou and has now culminated in a historic fourth-place finish in Aichi-Nagoya.
Article Summary: India fielded 167 athletes — 111 men and 56 women — across 11 sports at Aichi- Nagoya. India finished the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games with 114 medals — 30 gold, 35 silver and 49 bronze — to secure fourth place. It is the best finish in the country's history at the event.

That is where he took the game. So, it was not my best day, I would assume. I would always love to win a gold medal. So, yes, I am a little sad from that angle,” he said.The defeat also reminded him of how important it is to perform under pressure at major tournaments.“It is the most important factor to win medals at major games because you might be training well, you might actually have the fitness and the skills. But if you don't recreate that during the major games, then probably it is of not much use in terms of professional success,” Suhas said.Suhas, an IAS officer, said he had never imagined representing India in international badminton a decade ago.In November 2016, he made his debut at the Asian Championships in Beijing and won gold. Since then, he has won several medals at major international events. These include bronze at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta, silver at the Tokyo 2020 Paralympics, another silver at the Paris 2024 Paralympics, gold at the Hangzhou Asian Para Games and bronze in Nagoya.The 43-year-old has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024, winning silver on both occasions.With the Los Angeles 2028 Paralympics approaching, the big question is whether he can go one step further and win gold.The desire is there, but Suhas is not looking too far ahead. He wants to take things one step at a time.“If you had asked me 10 years ago, I didn't even know that I would play for India. But whenever I look at the medals and the love I have got from fans and sportspersons around the world, the journey has been quite satisfying. I have had the honour of wearing the Indian jersey and winning medals for my country,” he said.“I am grateful for what God has given me. I never imagined that I would become an IAS officer one day, an Arjuna awardee or a badminton player winning medals for India. I never imagined all this. But thanks to the Almighty for all these,” Suhas, who is also an Arjuna Award recipient, said.“So if God and destiny have been kind to me, I hope they will take me to a place that I deserve. I hope I can do the best that I can in whatever I choose to,” he added.For most people, the end of a hectic working day is a time to relax, spend time with family, play with their children or watch a movie.For Suhas, it is often time to pick up his badminton racket and head to the court. His day includes early-morning gym sessions, office work, inspections, meetings, video conferences and checking files. Despite his demanding responsibilities as an IAS officer, he makes time for badminton and follows a strict fitness routine to compete at the highest level.Balancing the two careers is not easy, but his love for the sport keeps him going.“If you choose what you love, then the journey becomes painless. You enjoy that journey. That's what I do,” Suhas said.Explaining how he manages his work and training, he said: “It is challenging. My training generally starts in the night and it always involves sacrifices. Probably others would be spending time with their family members or having leisure time. My leisure time is to play badminton. In badminton, you need an extremely high level of fitness. It's challenging, hectic but at the same time I love it.”“I don't remember eating sweets in the last many months. I can't recall when I had my last sweet. So, I almost don't eat sweets or fried food and am also quite conscious about the nutrition that I take,” he said.Suhas grew up watching Malaysian badminton great Lee Chong Wei and was inspired by his movement on the court.“Yes, I have always been inspired by so many top players in the able-bodied category. Growing up, I watched the matches of Lee Chong Wei and how he used to move around the court,” he said.“Even in India, the top shuttlers perform extremely well, whether it is Lakshya Sen, HS Prannoy or Kidambi Srikanth. I know them personally and have always admired how well they are able to compete at the top,” Suhas signed off.
Article Summary: Suhas Yathiraj was disappointed with his bronze medal at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya. The Indian shuttler lost the men's singles SL4 semifinal 23- 21, 8-21, 15-21. Suhas has represented India at two Paralympic Games, Tokyo in 2020 and Paris in 2024.
